en.name: Eucharistic Miracle of Seefeld
en.summary: A nobleman who insisted on receiving the larger host reserved for clergy reportedly sank into the church floor before the host began to bleed.
en.body: According to tradition, a wealthy Tyrolean nobleman named Oswald Milser attended Holy Thursday Mass at the parish church of Seefeld, Austria, in 1384, and, wishing to display his status, demanded that the priest give him the large host normally reserved for the celebrant rather than the smaller host given to lay communicants. As he received it, the ground beneath him is said to have opened and begun swallowing him, while the host in his mouth began to bleed, terrifying him into immediate repentance; he was reportedly saved only after fervent prayer, though the experience left him permanently changed, and he went on to found a nearby monastery in penance. An indentation in the church floor is still shown to visitors as a mark of the event, and the relic is preserved in the parish church, which remains a regional pilgrimage site.
